title: 30s outbound presence rate limit hardcoded
description:
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md
Line: 533

Current text:
  "On success, the remote server MAY push subsequent `Peer/presence` calls to the subscriber whenever the owner's presence, statusText, or statusEmoji changes. Servers SHOULD rate-limit outbound `Peer/presence` calls per subscriber to no more than one call per 30 seconds. Servers MAY drop presence push deliveries that fail; presence delivery is best-effort."

Because presence push is explicitly best-effort and the receiver has no rate contract, the 30-second figure is not wire-observable. A subscriber receives whatever rate the publisher chooses; nothing breaks if one publisher sends every 10s and another every 5 minutes. The number is a deployment-side cost-control parameter.

Suggested rewording:
  "Servers SHOULD rate-limit outbound `Peer/presence` calls per subscriber; the specific rate is implementation-defined."

Note: the typing rate-limit at federation line 393-396 (3 seconds) is consistent with the main chat draft's Chat/typing limit at line 931; that's a different judgment call (whether to soften both consistently) and is tracked separately under jmap-chat-spec-uy1m if pursued. This bead only covers the 30-second presence number, which has no equivalent anchor in the main draft.
acceptance_criteria:
- The "30 seconds" number is removed from line 533
- The SHOULD rate-limit obligation is retained, but the specific rate is impl-defined
- Best-effort delivery language is retained
- No change to the typing rate-limit at federation line 393-396 (different judgment call)
